description:
A signed write or delete against a path inside a channel directory, published as a `$type`-tagged record on the channel's main envelope stream. The substrate's invariant #8 (everything is a file; the channel directory is the activation surface) makes the channel-dir the unit of sync — envelopes are one kind of file, but `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/skills/*.md`, `template.md`, `contract.md`, `channel.md` are all files too, and they ride the same per-channel ordered append-only log. Replay walks all `$type: fileUpdate` records ordered by `effectiveAt` then record TID, applying last-writer-wins per path. No CRDT merge — concurrent writes are resolved by the sequencer's ordering (project_no_crdt_in_core).

Large content (>~4KB) is uploaded to the relay's content-addressed blob store first and referenced via `blobRef`; small content rides inline. Either `contentInline` or `blobRef` MUST be present when `op == write`; both MUST be absent when `op == delete`. `contentHash` is the blake3 hash of the canonical content bytes, used for integrity check on inline content and for retrieval on blob_ref content.

**Path discipline.** Path validation runs at BOTH the relay (refuses to enqueue) and the subscriber (refuses to write) — belt-and-suspenders, the cost of getting this wrong is local filesystem escape. Refused paths: absolute (leading `/`), any `..` traversal component, anything matching `*.local.md` (private-by-extension per AGENTS.md rule #6, never on the wire), anything inside `.git/`, and anything that resolves outside the channel-dir.

**Skill quarantine.** Per the v0.8 channel-relay-sequencer pitch, subscriber daemons receiving a fileUpdate writing into `.claude/skills/*.md` divert the write to `.claude/skills.incoming/` instead — the principal explicitly promotes via `mv` before the skill auto-activates. This is enforced subscriber-side; the wire shape is identical.

signer.description: DID of the principal authoring this file mutation. Must match the verifying key the signature checks against AND MUST hold the `publish` role on the target channel (admin role required for `.claude/`, `CLAUDE.md`, and `template.md` writes — the channel-context surface; deferred enforcement, v0.4).

op.description: The mutation kind. `write` creates or replaces the file at `path` with the carried content. `delete` removes the file at `path`. Subscribers MUST tolerate `delete` on a path that doesn't exist locally (idempotent).

path.description: Channel-dir-relative path to the file, forward-slash separated (e.g. `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/skills/review.md`, `template.md`, `contract.md`). MUST be a relative path: no leading `/`, no `..` components, no `.local.md` suffix on any segment, nothing inside `.git/`. Path validation runs on the relay at enqueue time AND on the subscriber at receive time.

contentInline.description: Inline content bytes for `op == write`. Use when content is small (suggested threshold ~4KB). Mutually exclusive with `blobRef`. Encoded base64 on the wire.

blobRef.description: Content-addressed reference to a blob stored on the relay, of the form `blake3:<hex>`. Use when content is large. Mutually exclusive with `contentInline`. Subscribers fetch the blob via `GET /blobs/<hex>` on the channel's relay and verify the returned bytes hash to the referenced digest before writing.

contentHash.description: Blake3 hash of the canonical content bytes for `op == write`, formatted as `blake3:<hex>`. For `contentInline`, MUST match the hash of the decoded bytes. For `blobRef`, MUST equal the `blobRef` value (the blob's content-addressed key). Required for `op == write`; absent for `op == delete`. Canonicalization: bytes are written verbatim — no BOM strip, no CRLF normalization, no trailing whitespace strip (we preserve what the author wrote).

effectiveAt.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp from which the mutation takes effect. Verifiers SHOULD reject mutations with `effectiveAt` in the future beyond a reasonable skew. Replays are ordered by this field then by record TID; last-writer-wins per path.

note.description: Optional free-form note (e.g. `Updated review skill with new TDD prompt`). Not interpreted by the protocol.

signature.description: Detached ed25519 signature over the canonical bytes of (op, path, contentHash, effectiveAt). Format: `ed25519:<base64>` with 64 raw bytes. Canonicalization rule: concatenate the listed fields as UTF-8 strings separated by U+001F (unit separator). For `op == delete`, `contentHash` is empty in the canonical preimage (it's absent from the record). Note that `blobRef` and `contentInline` are NOT in the signed preimage — they're alternate carriers of the bytes whose hash IS signed, so an attacker who swaps carrier without changing bytes can't break the signature, and an attacker who swaps bytes invalidates `contentHash`.
